newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria offers incentives to end gas flaring.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria offers incentives to end gas flaring.

text.p: Nigeria will offer incentives including tax relief to oil companies that use, rather than flare off, natural gas, finance minister Anthony Ani said.
Operators would enjoy tax relief for three years, renewable for three further years subject to satisfactory performance, Ani said in a briefing to the business community on the 1997 budget.
Nigeria has more gas reserves than crude oil but 80 percent of its gas is flared during the production of crude oil.
Last November the government set a 2010 deadline to stop gas flaring in order to curb environmental pollution.
Other incentives, Ani said, would be accelerated capital allowances for investments in plant machinery and additional investment allowance of 15 percent but which would not reduce value of the asset.

Investments necessary to separate oil and gas from the reservoir into usable products and investments in facilities to deliver associated gas in usable form will be considered part of capital investments for oil field development, Ani said.
The Nigerian subsidiaries of Royal/Dutch Shell, Mobil Corp and Chevron Corp are already carrying out gas gathering projects aimed at reducing gas flaring.
Nigeria is also constructing a $4 liquefied natural gas plant, Africa's biggest project, in the southeastern town of Bonny which is expected to come onstream in 1999.
